sources.entry: Safelight - Open-source menu bar app that schedules the color filter, brightness, and Light/Dark appearance, fading the screen to deep red at night. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/mopfaff/Safelight) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Safelight is an open-source macOS menu bar app that runs one schedule for the color filter, brightness, Light/Dark appearance and wallpaper, fading the screen to deep red at night.
summary.what_it_does: Safelight lets you set how the screen should look at several times of day and fades between them. It drives the macOS Color Tint filter, so the screen can go fully red, and it sets brightness per display, including dimming external monitors and Sidecar iPads in software. Each time of day can also switch the system between Light and Dark appearance and pick a Light or Dark wallpaper that fades as the appearance changes. A strip along the top previews the whole day. Safelight changes the same settings System Settings does rather than drawing over the screen. It checks for updates daily through Sparkle, with an option to turn that off.
use_cases: reduce blue light and eye strain at night
schedule a red screen late in the evening
automatically switch Light and Dark mode by time of day
dim external monitors on a schedule
how_to_run: Download the Safelight .dmg from the latest release and drag Safelight to Applications.
Open Safelight; it is not notarized, so click Done when macOS warns.
Open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway next to Safelight.
Requires macOS 15.5 or later (Apple silicon or Intel).
To build: git clone the repository, cd Safelight, run scripts/release.sh (requires Xcode 26 or later).
Or open Safelight.xcodeproj in Xcode and run it.
notable: Uses the macOS Color Tint filter so the screen can go fully red, which Night Shift cannot do
Per-display brightness, with software dimming for displays that don't accept hardware brightness control
Wallpaper fades between Light and Dark pictures when the appearance changes
Labels come from System Settings' own translations, so the app appears in the Mac's language
Calls private System Settings functions, so it is not on the Mac App Store
caveats: Not notarized by Apple, so macOS blocks the first launch and needs manual approval in Privacy & Security
Relies on functions outside Apple's public APIs; a macOS update could break them
Requires macOS 15.5 or later and Xcode 26 to build; per-display brightness keys need Accessibility permission
Aerial wallpapers cannot move and shuffle options are not available
